text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:

- U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato, the World Jewish Congress and other organisations presented two documents they save prove that The Swiss National Bank sent 280 truckloads of looted Nazi gold to Spain and Portugal during World War Two. The gold was worth between one and two billion Swiss francs, according to a secret document from the former American secret service.
- Italian finance police confiscated some 75.5 billion Italian lira illegally transported across the Italian-Swiss border in 1996.
- Union Bank of Switzerland's president Robert Studer said in an interview that he views the danger of a boycott against Swiss banks as minor.
- Otto Piller, new director of the Swiss department of Social Insurance, said in an interview with Swiss television that insurance premiums must be frozen at the current level.

- A two-man balloon flown by Swiss Bertrand Piccard and Belgian Wim Verstraeten, built to make the first-ever round-the-world flight, came down in the Mediterranean on Sunday only six hours after it took off in the Swiss Alps.
